title: The Jo Adell era comes to a disappointing end for Angels: MLB trade grades
content:
The Athletic has live coverage of the 2026 MLB Trade Deadline.

Angels get: C Jacob Cozart

Guardians get: OF Jo Adell

Angels: B
Guardians: B+

For a player with Adell’s ceiling (37 homers last year!), pedigree (10th pick in 2017 and one of baseball’s top prospects thereafter), highlight-reel talent (did you see those three home-run robberies?) and contract status (under club control through next season), the Angels would have hoped to fetch more for him when they finally parted ways. But this is it.

After 10 seasons in the Angels organization, Adell is who he is — a corner outfielder with clear flaws both offensively and defensively. That’s not a player the industry values greatly.

Cozart is a helpful depth option for a team that just traded away catcher Logan O’Hoppe. But is he anything more than that? The Athletic’s Keith Law ranked Cozart as the Guardians’ No. 16 prospect this spring, writing that he projects as “a solid backup catcher who can defend and will get to enough power to be a long-term big leaguer.” Some evaluators think the bat will never be major-league caliber.

The Guardians are all set at catcher. In fact, Cozart is the second catcher they’ve sent away ahead of the trade deadline. Drafted in the second round in 2024 out of North Carolina State, the lefty-hitting Cozart has a .692 OPS in pro ball. Before the trade, he was slashing .239/.330/.384 at Double-A Akron. A backup catcher who can run into some homers and possibly play the strong side of a platoon? That sounds about right. — Stephen J. Nesbitt

Angels: A-
Guardians: B+

Everyone wanted the Adell era in Anaheim to work out over the course of this seven-year roller coaster. There were times when it looked like the former top prospect just might live up to his potential.

But ultimately, Adell was having a bad season for the Angels. He had a .287 on-base percentage, which included 16 walks and 108 strikeouts. His power was severely sapped. His sprint speed has cratered. His defense and arm strength ranked among the lowest in baseball.

The Guardians get a right-handed power bat who can hit left-handed pitching at a very high level. A player who’s still young, has an additional year of control, and might benefit from the superior coaching in Cleveland’s organization.

Against left-handed pitching this season, Adell has a .910 OPS, compared with .593 against righties. That is a very valuable asset in a playoff chase.

The Angels get a young catcher — an area of need following the trade of the struggling O’Hoppe. Is Cozart the catcher of the future in Anaheim? He may at least be part of the solution. He’s a strong defender who has struggled offensively. Interim general manager John Mozeliak has stated that getting a young catcher is a priority, and this deal fills that need. — Sam Blum
